title: Canonical relative ringed-site bidual evaluation transpose
statement: Let $C$ be a category with object universe $c$ and morphism universe $v$, $J$ a Grothendieck topology on $C$, and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings in universe $\max(c,v,r)$. Use sheafification and local-bijection identification for additive sheaves in that universe, the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D$ with morphisms in universe $w$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and its derived internal-Hom bifunctor $H$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $M$ be a normalized ringed-site duality model [def-zl-ringed-site-duality-model], with its closed tensor-Hom adjunction $S$ and Koszul symmetry $\sigma$. For any target $K\in D$ and any $P\in D$, define the relative bidual map $b_{K,P}:P\to H(H(P,K),K)$ to be the transpose under $S$ of the composite $P\otimes^L H(P,K)\xrightarrow{\sigma_{P,H(P,K)}}H(P,K)\otimes^L P\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_{P,K}}K$. Keep its naturality in $P$: for every $f:P\to P\prime$, $b_{K,P\prime}\circ f=H(H(f,1_K),1_K)\circ b_{K,P}$, where both occurrences of the first argument of $H$ are contravariant. This defines the canonical transformation from the identity to the relative double dual. The target $K$ is arbitrary; no invertibility of $b_{K,P}$ is required.
